phase3_findings.description: sw_denied uses substring match on the denial tool-name field (line 168). For the SHIP-gating denial predicate the permissive direction leans dangerous: a hypothetical sibling tool whose name contains 'schedulewakeup' (e.g. ScheduleWakeupV2) would gate DENIED/REMOVED. Small blast radius (no such tool known; outcome only adds a --disallowedTools flag). Consider exact/word-boundary match on the denial side while keeping the attempt predicate permissive.

denial_names collected only when permission_denials is a list (line 133). A single-dict shape would miss the denial name -> fails in the SAFE direction (INCONCLUSIVE/AVAILABLE, never a false ship). Note-only; harness record shape still unconfirmed.

matcher-probe.yml verdict-rationale + AWAITING RE-MEASUREMENT comment block (~30 lines) exceeds the three-line prevention-only comment cap and is largely provenance/derivation. Plausibly covered by the load-bearing-undecidable carve-out (probe-of-record documenting a withdrawn measurement + RE-PROBE instruction). All claims accurate against HEAD.

Several reworded test-arm rationale comments in review-stall-backstop.sh sit at or slightly over the three-line cap with worked-example/fixture-narration prose. Most name a concrete regression the arm guards (compliant shape). Accuracy verified.

Denial-name lookup honors ('tool','tool_name','name') but only 'tool' and 'tool_name' have fixtures. Dropping 'name' from the tuple leaves every arm green (a partial fail-open), and the arm comment claims dropping 'tool_name'/'name' would regress the arm. Add a REMOVED fixture whose denial entry is {"name":"ScheduleWakeup"}. Low severity (3/10) — real harness field still unmeasured.
